title: Kayla Carrera
summary: Episode 62 is an emergency Friday-the-13th recording centered on a newly hired engineer's sexual encounter with retired adult performer Kayla Carrera immediately before the show. It moves from the cast's hotel photo shoot and the 2013 adult-industry HIV moratorium into a minute reconstruction of the encounter, condom use, erectile difficulty, public humiliation, orientation speculation, employer-directed sexual experiments, and audience recruitment of future dates. The employee eventually says that if the show will discuss him, he must appear to defend himself. That statement, combined with third-day employment, alcohol, host planning, and broadcast expectation, prevents the archive from treating participation as uncomplicated consent. The closing sections include private college stories, a no that was respected, health-podcast claims, trivia, and a lesion-smelling penalty.
sensitivity: Explicit sexual content; workplace sexual pressure; alcohol and consent; adult-industry labor; HIV rumor and medical privacy; condom misuse; erectile-function diagnosis and medication; orientation slurs; implant injury; private partners and family; identifiable college acquaintances; public humiliation; treated lesion exposure.
speaker_policy: Named dialogue remains withheld. Episode 62 has 2,433 fixed-window embeddings but zero diarized turns, and no independently validated held-out multi-speaker test has passed. Guest and cast introductions support episode structure, not publishable acoustic attribution.
